body: Logic bug: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires the user to be an OWNER (isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER), so team admins are denied. This should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin` alone. Also, `teamId ?? 0` runs two pointless DB queries for non-team bookings.

Any attendee, not only the organizer or a team admin, can add an unlimited number of arbitrary email addresses. The server then sends them booking invitations from the organizer's name and pushes them into the organizer's calendar event. This is a spam/abuse vector. Consider limiting this to the organizer and team admins, or capping the number of guests. The email comparison is also case-sensitive.

The booking status and time are never checked. Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings, which re-sends 'scheduled' invites and ICS REQUESTs for a meeting that isn't happening. Seated events (seatsPerTimeSlot) are also not handled: adding plain attendees to a seated booking bypasses seat limits and BookingSeat records.

The blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not, so `Foo@blocked.com` gets past the blacklist. The duplicate check against existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added a second time with different casing. Normalize both sides with toLowerCase(). Duplicates within the input itself are only rejected on the client, never on the server.
`booking.userId || 0` together with `findFirstOrThrow` turns a booking with no user into an unhandled Prisma NotFound error (a 500) instead of a proper TRPCError.

EventManager is built with the requesting user's credentials (`ctx.user`), not the booking organizer's. When a team admin or an attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees tries to update the organizer's calendar and video references using the wrong user's credentials. That either fails or doesn't find the event, so the organizer's calendar never gets the new guests. Use `booking.user` with its credentials instead (booking.user.credentials is already included in the query).

The attendees are already saved to the DB before this call, and it is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws (e.g. expired credentials), the client sees an error even though the guests were added, and no emails are sent. A retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Handle the error, or do the DB write and the external sync consistently.

The emails are sent with the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. Any submitted email that was already an attendee then gets a full 'new booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`. Also, the caught error is swallowed without being logged.
No bounds on `guests`: an empty array is accepted, and so is an unbounded list, which lets one request trigger many outbound emails. Add `.min(1)` and a reasonable `.max(...)`.

For recurring bookings, only this single occurrence is updated. The new guests are missing from the other occurrences in the DB, while the calendar update and ICS may cover the whole series (evt.recurringEvent is set), which leaves the two inconsistent.

`message` is a template literal that is never empty (e.g. 'undefined: ...'), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be used. Separately, `isInvalidEmail` is never reset after the user fixes their input or after a successful submit, so the error message stays visible.

`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is a case-sensitive exact match against the raw client input. Combined with the handler passing `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`, existing attendees can receive the wrong email template.
